title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Datadog
providers.scope_notes: IP documentation differs on entitlement (Pro+ via support vs Enterprise). Confirm contract. AWS WIF requires supported integration/configuration.

controls.name: Client Tokens Write permission
controls.what: Only roles with client_tokens_write can create or edit client tokens (Standard role by default).
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles; Organization Settings > Client Tokens

no_control.what: No expiration for RUM client tokens, and they survive deactivation of the creating user.
no_control.quote: When a user who created a client token is deactivated, the client token remains active.

controls_unknown: No org setting found that blocks personal application keys or forces service-account-only keys.

Whether the IP allowlist applies to API-key and client-token requests outside telemetry intake is not stated; entitlement differs between account docs (Pro+/Enterprise) and API reference (Enterprise).
Plan requirement for Agent-based WIF: current WIF page lists no tier; earlier material says Enterprise-only and preview.
How to delete or disable an identity mapping is not documented on the WIF page; intake mappings are deleted via API.
Whether custom roles (needed to narrow these permissions) require a specific plan was not confirmed.

authentication.summary: Org-level token set as clientToken in browser and mobile SDKs to submit RUM events and logs. It is meant to be visible client-side, unlike API keys.

federation.details: Static public token embedded in client code; no external identity exchange applies.

ip_restriction.boundary: The org IP allowlist (Pro+ or Enterprise, via support) covers the UI and API but excludes data ingest endpoints. Client-token intake is not named either way; since end-user browsers send this traffic, source-IP limits would not normally fit.

renewal.summary: The token is reused until deleted; rotate by creating a new token and updating the client.

administration.summary: Client Tokens Write (default Standard role) creates and edits tokens; Read Only role can view them. RUM applications get a client token automatically. Deleted tokens cannot be restored.
administration.conditions: Tokens stay active after the creating user is deactivated, so review them separately from user offboarding. An authenticated proxy can hide the token from end users.

offboard.details: Client tokens stay active when the user who created them is deactivated.

inventory.details: Organization Settings > Client Tokens tab lists the org's client tokens.

token_format.notes: Not covered by GitHub secret scanning patterns; format not documented.

log_sources.name: Organization Settings > Client Tokens
log_sources.notes: Lists tokens; no documented usage logging

log_sources.name: Datadog Audit Trail
log_sources.notes: May record @asset.type:public_api_key events; not confirmed to be client tokens.

anomaly_cues: Spike in RUM sessions or browser logs from unexpected application names or origins
Logs/RUM ingestion volume or cost spike tied to one token
Client token reused in an app it was not issued for

containment.steps: Delete the token in Organization Settings > Client Tokens and ship a new token in the SDK config.
containment.notes: Deletion is permanent; deactivating the creator does not disable it. Token is public by design, so treat as abuse/injection risk, not secret leak.

sample_query.purpose: Org Settings access/creation/deletion of public API keys (may cover client tokens; unconfirmed)

unknown: audit event name for client token create/delete
